intro: A Michigan trio of whimsical, cello-laced folk.
story: Breathe Owl Breathe is Micah Middaugh, Andréa Moreno-Beals and Trevor Hobbs of East Jordan, Michigan, who live together in a log cabin; the band began in 2004, when Moreno-Beals was an Oberlin freshman. They played Pickathon in 2009, 2010, 2011 and again in 2013. That November Under the Radar wrote that they had finally decided to grow up on Passage of Pegasus. They keep pairing music with visual art, and in December 2026 announced a winter concert alongside their traveling exhibition Oval Realms.

intro: A soul duo of Nicole Wray and Terri Walker.
story: Lady was the duo of the R&B singers Nicole Wray, from Portsmouth, Virginia, and Terri Walker of London, who met in New York in 2009 and bonded over classic soul. They toured as Lee Fields and the Expressions' backing vocalists in 2012, and their self-titled debut came out on Truth & Soul in March 2013, with NPR's Oliver Wang praising how their voices weave under and atop one another. They played Pickathon that year. Walker left, and Wray continued as Lady Wray, with Queen Alone on Big Crown on September 23, 2016, and Cover Girl in 2025.

Sarah Versprille and Daniel Hindman formed Pure Bathing Culture in 2011, after moving from Brooklyn to Portland; they also toured with Vetiver. Stereogum named them a Band to Watch on June 27, 2013, and Moon Tides, recorded in ten days at Richard Swift's studio, came out on Partisan on August 20, the summer of their Pickathon set. Pray for Rain followed in 2015, and in November 2025 they released the single I Said What I Said on Father/Daughter Records.

Ishmael Butler of Digable Planets founded Shabazz Palaces in Seattle in 2009, and first appeared as Palaceer Lazaro; Sub Pop signed them in September 2010, its first hip-hop signing. Black Up came out on Sub Pop on June 28, 2011, and Slant said it shows an artist carving his own path. They played Pickathon in 2013, returned in 2015 and released Lese Majesty in 2014. Their eighth album, It's A Style Sport, came out on Sub Pop in October 2026.
